lines.text: On the night before the Remeasuring, the King gave a feast. Lanterns in the palace gardens, music, and more five-ring heirs than stars.
Prince Aurelio spent the whole evening courting Princess Mirelle. He gave her a Calvere sword with a blade like rippling water. He gave her a poem. He gave her a white horse.
Marry me, Princess, and the Calvere fleet is yours. Every ship, every sail. Think how safe your uncle's coast would be.
I'd rather your fleet stayed on its own side of the sea, Highness. Keep the poem. The horse can stay.
I don't know why I was glad she said no. It was none of my business. I told myself that twice.
Later, the prince found me alone on the terrace. There had been frost on the flagstones all evening. Except where I was standing.
Lord Lucan. Your hands are cold, but the air around you is warm. Did you know? The frost runs from your boots like a frightened cat.
In Calvere, we'd say you were touched by the sun. Here, I think they say something else.
Here, they say I'm a zero.
Tomorrow, we'll see.
I didn't hear what happened next. I only learned it long afterwards, from the last person I would have expected to tell me.
In a dark pavilion at the bottom of the garden, Lady Sabine was waiting for him.
Everything I know about the boy, Highness. His village, his wolf, his friends. And what the Order means to do to him tomorrow.
And you're certain? He's truly hollow-born?
I've watched him for a year. Nobody who stands near that boy stays common.
He paid her in Calvere gold. A great deal of it.
For fifty years, Lady Sabine, my father has kept the Order rich. And the Order has sold him hollow-born glass. Rings. Lamps. Little bottles.
My father is tired of buying glass. He would like the spring.
Vance will never sell him.
Vance sells everything. He just hasn't been offered enough. And if his Stone empties the boy tomorrow? Well. Empty springs come cheaper.
And if it doesn't?
Then I'll know he's clever. I like clever things. I collect them.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter seventy-eight, coming soon.
